editorial:
Imagine being so heartbroken that you decide to make a movie just to find your ex. That is exactly what happens here. You follow a shoe salesman from New York who is totally lost after a breakup. He decides to film a video message to the world, hoping someone recognizes his old flame. To show why things went wrong, he hires a grumpy actress to play the ex-girlfriend. The vibe is light and funny, but it also feels very real because you get to see him mess up over and over again. It is like watching a guy try to fix his life while accidentally exposing every flaw he has in front of a camera.

What really works is the chemistry between the lead and the actress. Watching her tear into him and point out his mistakes is the best part of the whole ride. The pacing stays snappy, though some of the indie filmmaking style might feel a bit raw. If you enjoy stories about growth and awkward romance, you should definitely give this a shot.
endingExplained: By the end, the main character realizes that his quest to find his ex was actually about forgiving himself. He stops obsessing over the past after the actress helps him see his own faults. Instead of getting his old girlfriend back, he finds peace with the breakup. The movie wraps up with him finally moving on, proving that the process of making the film was the real cure for his broken heart.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves awkward romantic comedies and stories about self-discovery.
